summary: Lockwood Lake tower: listed on a Saskatchewan fire-tower page with a position only; no build, staffing, status or access source found.

evidence.supports: Lockwood Lake position on the card; the card gives no height, year, towermen or notes
Department began building fire control towers across northern Saskatchewan at about fifty-mile intervals
evidence.quote: The Department of Natural Resources soon began constructing fire control towers at approximately fifty-mile intervals across northern Saskatchewan.

evidence.supports: Spacing was chosen so that radio contact could be made between tower men
evidence.quote: This distance was chosen to assure that radio contact could be made between tower men.

evidence.supports: Towers ranged from 35 to 100 feet and were built of wood or steel
evidence.quote: The height of the towers varied from between thirty-five and one hundred feet. They were constructed of either wood or steel.

evidence.supports: Same fire finder, two-way radio and field glasses in every tower, as in all other towers
evidence.quote: The equipment in the tower, as in all other towers, consisted of a fire finder, two-way radio, and a pair of field glasses.

evidence.supports: The history was submitted by Arnold Fonos
The page is about the Big River district and the province's towers generally, not Lockwood Lake
evidence.quote: Towers and Saskatchewan Environment - Big River and Area

sources.title: Towers and Saskatchewan Environment - Big River and Area

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. No firelookout.ca entry was found for Lockwood Lake (slugs lockwood-lake-fire-tower, lockwood-lake-tower and lockwood-fire-tower all return 404). The card coordinates match the record (55-37.8125 X 109-13.1250 = 55.63021, -109.21875), so no correction. The JKCC history covers the Big River district and towers in general and never names this tower, so it is used for network context only. The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency, formerly DNR) is not supported by any source read for this tower; the JKCC text says the Department of Natural Resources built the network, which is not a statement about this site. Search budget was exceeded: three searches were run for this tower against a limit of two.
